title: Book Features and Author's Reasons
keyIdea: A book has a front cover with the title and a picture, a spine down the side, and a back cover with the blurb, which tells you what the book is about. Inside, the title page names the title, the author, who writes the words, and the illustrator, who draws the pictures. In an information book, the author makes a point and gives reasons that back it up. A reason shows the point is right; a true fact that does not show this is not a reason.

kid: Look at a book. The front cover is what you see first. It has the title and a big picture. The spine is the thin side. On a shelf, you see the spine.
Turn the book over. That is the back cover. The short bit of writing there is the blurb. It tells you what the book is about.
Open the book. The title page has the title again. It names the author, who wrote the words. It names the illustrator, who drew the pictures.

Books that teach facts make a point, like "Bees are helpful." Then they give reasons. "Bees make honey" is a reason. "Bees have six legs" is true, but it does not show bees help us. So it is not a reason for that point.
adult: Five to eight is when children move from enjoying books to knowing how they work. This topic covers the parts of a book (front cover, back cover, spine, blurb and title page), the roles named on the title page (author and illustrator), and an early reading-for-meaning skill from information texts: finding the reasons an author gives to support a point.

In the US Common Core these are standards RI.K.5 and RI.K.6 (parts of a book, author and illustrator) and RI.1.8 and RI.2.8 (identify the reasons an author gives to support points). In England they sit in Year 1 and Year 2 reading: discussing the title and how items of information are related, and learning how non-fiction books are structured. A point is the main claim; a reason is a sentence that shows the claim is right.

Common mistakes to watch for: mixing up the author and the illustrator; looking for the blurb on the front cover; calling any true fact a reason even when it does not support the point, such as "bees have six legs" for "bees are helpful"; and offering an opinion such as "I like frogs" as a reason. Be careful to praise a true fact before explaining why it does not back up this point.

In the lab your child drags labels onto a book's front cover, spine, back cover and blurb, taps the title, author and illustrator on a title page, picks the three sentences that show bees are helpful, sorts dog facts under the point they support, and builds point because reason sentences.

familyTip: At bedtime, before you read, ask your child to find the front cover, the spine and the blurb, then the author and illustrator on the title page. With an information book, read one page and ask, "What is the author's point? Which sentence backs it up?" Use the word because: "Bees are helpful because they make honey."

visual.caption: Point: bees are helpful. Is each line a reason for it? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: label a book's covers, spine and blurb, find the title, author and illustrator, then spot and sort an author's reasons.

practice.prompt: Where is the blurb on a book?
practice.hint: Turn the book over. Where is the short bit that tells you what the book is about?
practice.explain: The blurb is on the back cover. It tells you what the book is about, so you can choose if you want to read it.

practice.prompt: A book has {n} pictures. Who drew them?
practice.hint: One person writes the words. Another person can draw the pictures. Which name is for the pictures?
practice.explain: The illustrator drew all {n} pictures. The author wrote the words. You find both names on the title page.

practice.prompt: Point: Dogs are good helpers. Which is a reason?
choices: Dogs can guide people who cannot see
I saw a dog in the park
practice.hint: A reason shows the point is right. Which one shows dogs help people?
practice.explain: Guiding people who cannot see shows dogs help. Four legs is true but does not show helping, and seeing a dog is not a reason.

practice.prompt: There are {n} books on a shelf. Which part of each book can you see?
practice.hint: On a shelf, books stand side by side. Which part faces out?
practice.explain: On a shelf you see each spine, so all {n} spines show their titles. The blurb is on the back and the title page is inside.

pool.prompt: What is on the front cover of a book?
choices: The title and a big picture
pool.hint: What do you see first when you pick up a book?
pool.explain: The front cover shows the title and a big picture. The blurb is on the back cover.

pool.prompt: Who writes the words in a book?
pool.hint: One name is for the words, one is for the pictures.
pool.explain: The author writes the words. The illustrator draws the pictures. The spine is a part of the book, not a person.

pool.prompt: Where can you find the title, the author and the illustrator together?
pool.hint: Open the book. Which page near the front names the people who made it?
pool.explain: The title page, just inside the book, names the title, the author and the illustrator.

pool.prompt: Point: Trees are important. Which is a reason?
pool.hint: Does it show trees matter? A true fact is not always a reason.
pool.explain: Clean air shows trees are important. Being tall is true, but it does not show trees matter.

pool.prompt: A page about frogs has {n} sentences. Which one backs up "Frogs need water"?
pool.hint: Which sentence tells you why frogs need water?
pool.explain: Of the {n} sentences, "their skin must stay wet" is the reason. Green is a fact that does not explain it, and liking frogs is an opinion.

pool.prompt: An author gives {n} reasons that bees help us. What do the reasons do?
pool.hint: Why does an author add reasons after a point?
pool.explain: All {n} reasons back up the point that bees help us. They show the point is right.

pool.prompt: Which sentence uses because to join a point and a reason?
choices: We brush our teeth because it stops holes
We brush our teeth because I have a red brush
We brush our teeth and it is Monday
pool.hint: The part after because must show why the point is right.
pool.explain: Stopping holes is why we brush our teeth. A red brush and Monday do not explain the point.
